## Garbage in, garbage out

A surrogate model does not know that a value is wrong. It learns it.

| Problem | Example | Effect on a model |
|---|---|---|
| wrong unit | load in kN in some rows | learns a fake relationship |
| typo | thickness 196 mm instead of 19.6 | one point pulls the fit |
| failed run | stress = 0 | "infinitely safe" designs |
| duplicates | same run exported twice | over-weights some designs, leaks into the test set |
| gaps | missing deflection | errors or silently dropped rows |

# Reading a messy export {.divider}

## First attempt

```{python}
raw = pd.read_csv("data/bracket_raw.csv")
raw.head(3)
```

One column only → the separator is not a comma.

## Second attempt

```{python}
raw = pd.read_csv("data/bracket_raw.csv", sep=";", decimal=",")
raw.head()
```

## What types did we get?

```{python}
raw.dtypes
```

- `load_N` and `max_stress_MPa` are **text**, although they should be numbers
- why? Some values use a dot, some a comma; some say `n/a`

```{python}
raw["max_stress_MPa"].head(6).tolist()
```

## Converting to numbers safely

```{python}
def to_number(col):
    """Text -> float; accepts decimal commas and dots, bad values become NaN."""
    return pd.to_numeric(col.astype(str).str.replace(",", "."), errors="coerce")

clean = raw.copy()
for c in ["load_N", "max_stress_MPa"]:
    clean[c] = to_number(clean[c])
clean.dtypes[["load_N", "max_stress_MPa"]]
```

- `errors="coerce"` turns anything that is not a number into `NaN` (missing)
- always work on a **copy** — keep the raw data untouched

# Missing values {.divider}

## Finding them

```{python}
clean.isna().sum()
```

```{python}
clean[clean.isna().any(axis=1)].head()
```

## What to do with missing values?

| Option | When | pandas |
|---|---|---|
| drop the row | few rows, the value is essential (an output) | `dropna(subset=[...])` |
| recompute | the value can be derived from others | e.g. SF = 355 / stress |
| fill with a known value | a default really applies | `fillna(value)` |
| fill with a statistic | only for inputs, only with care | `fillna(col.median())` |
| re-run the calculation | best, if possible | — |

::: {.tip}
Never fill a missing **output** (stress, deflection) with a mean: you invent a calculation
result. For training data, re-run or drop.
:::

## In our data

```{python}
# E is missing in a few rows: material is the same steel, 200 GPa is a defensible nominal value
clean["E_GPa"] = clean["E_GPa"].fillna(200.0)

# deflection is an output: we cannot invent it
before = len(clean)
clean = clean.dropna(subset=["deflection_mm"])
print(f"dropped {before - len(clean)} runs without deflection")
```

::: {.muted}
Write down every decision like this. It goes into the model passport later.
:::

```{python}
print(clean.duplicated().sum(), "identical rows")
print(clean["run_id"].duplicated().sum(), "repeated run IDs")
clean[clean["run_id"].duplicated(keep=False)].sort_values("run_id")
```

```{python}
clean = clean.drop_duplicates()
assert clean["run_id"].is_unique
```

::: {.muted}
Same ID but different values? That is not a duplicate — it is a conflict. Find out which one is right.

# Units and impossible values {.divider}

## Check ranges against physics and the plan

```{python}
clean[["thickness_mm", "fillet_radius_mm", "load_N", "E_GPa"]].describe().loc[["min", "max"]]
```

- negative thickness → sign error
- thickness 190 mm → probably a missing decimal point (plan was 8–20 mm)
- load around 1–3 → entered in **kN** instead of N (plan was 200–3000 N)

## Fixing what we understand

```{python}
in_kN = clean["load_N"] < 10
print(in_kN.sum(), "loads look like kN")
clean.loc[in_kN, "load_N"] = clean.loc[in_kN, "load_N"] * 1000

bad_t = ~clean["thickness_mm"].between(8, 20)
clean.loc[bad_t, ["run_id", "thickness_mm"]]
```

```{python}
clean = clean[~bad_t]      # unclear what the right value was -> remove and report
print(len(clean), "runs left")
```

::: {.muted}
Fix only what you can explain (kN → N is certain). If you would have to guess: exclude and flag for re-calculation.
:::

## Outliers: suspicious, not automatically wrong

```{python}
q1, q3 = clean["max_stress_MPa"].quantile([0.25, 0.75])
iqr = q3 - q1
far = clean[clean["max_stress_MPa"] > q3 + 1.5 * iqr]      # classic 1.5 × IQR rule
print(len(far), "runs far above the rest")
far[["run_id", "thickness_mm", "fillet_radius_mm", "load_N", "max_stress_MPa"]].head()
```

- statistical rule (IQR) finds candidates; **physics** decides
- thin plate + small radius + high load → high stress is real, keep it

# Failed calculations {.divider}

## Solver status and zero results

```{python}
clean["solver_status"].value_counts()
```

```{python}
clean[clean["solver_status"] != "converged"][["run_id", "max_stress_MPa", "safety_factor"]]
```

```{python}
clean = clean[clean["solver_status"] == "converged"]
clean = clean.dropna(subset=["max_stress_MPa"])
print(len(clean), "runs left")
```

## Consistency checks between columns

```{python}
recomputed = 355 / clean["max_stress_MPa"]
diff = (recomputed - clean["safety_factor"]).abs()
print("max difference:", round(diff.max(), 4))
```

- derived columns must agree with their sources
- physics: deflection should grow with load and fall with thickness — check later in EDA

# Making it repeatable {.divider}

## One cleaning function

```{python}
def clean_bracket(path):
    """Read and clean a raw bracket export. Returns (clean DataFrame, report dict)."""
    df = pd.read_csv(path, sep=";", decimal=",")
    report = {"rows_in": len(df)}
    for c in ["load_N", "max_stress_MPa"]:
        df[c] = to_number(df[c])
    df = df.drop_duplicates()
    df.loc[df["load_N"] < 10, "load_N"] *= 1000                      # kN -> N
    df["E_GPa"] = df["E_GPa"].fillna(200.0)
    df = df[df["solver_status"] == "converged"]
    df = df[df["thickness_mm"].between(8, 20)]
    df = df.dropna(subset=["max_stress_MPa", "deflection_mm"])
    df["safety_factor"] = 355 / df["max_stress_MPa"]                  # recompute, consistent
    report["rows_out"] = len(df)
    return df.reset_index(drop=True), report

data, rep = clean_bracket("data/bracket_raw.csv")
rep
```

## Checks that stop bad data

```{python}
def validate(df):
    assert df["run_id"].is_unique, "duplicate run IDs"
    assert df.notna().all().all(), "missing values left"
    assert df["thickness_mm"].between(8, 20).all(), "thickness out of plan range"
    assert df["load_N"].between(200, 3000).all(), "load out of plan range (unit?)"
    assert (df["max_stress_MPa"] > 0).all(), "non-positive stress"
    return True

validate(data)
```

::: {.tip}
Put `clean_bracket` and `validate` in a `.py` file and commit them. New export from the
solver → one line to get clean, checked data.
:::

## Summary

- read with the right `sep` and `decimal`; check `dtypes` first
- `pd.to_numeric(..., errors="coerce")` for mixed text/number columns
- missing values: never invent outputs; document what you filled and why
- duplicates: `duplicated`, `drop_duplicates`, unique IDs
- ranges: compare with the plan and with physics; fix only what you can explain
- one cleaning function + `assert` checks = repeatable
